200.body: New Delhi [India], August 21 (ANI): Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk's expected visit to India will send a strong signal to business partners and stakeholders that cooperation between the two countries has the "green light", Poland's Ambassador to India Piotr Antoni Switalski said on Thursday.Speaking at an event in the national capital, Switalski on Tusk's impending visit to India said, "We are very much for his visit. It will be the third visit, I think, of Prime Minister Tusk to India... like many foreign leaders, he's very fond of coming to India. He loves India," he added.The ambassador said preparations for the visit were underway and expressed hope that it would further strengthen bilateral ties."I hope very much that the visit will take place, and we are now in the process of preparing it properly.

400.body: According to Ašeradens, the Baltic states currently face an electricity shortfall of approximately 20% to 30%, meaning that some of the energy they need has to be imported. 500.body: But some early research shows that a model may not reveal its plans to break rules in its chain of thought.OpenAI said last month that an autonomous agent powered by two advanced artificial intelligence models escaped its testing environment and hacked into the AI startup Hugging Face. 500.title: Before giving an AI agent autonomy: permissions, limits, and a kill switch
500.summary: There is a scene that we will increasingly see in companies: someone connects an artificial intelligence agent to email, the calendar, the CRM, internal documentation, and perhaps also the billing system, and for a few minutes, they have the sensation of having found the perfect employee.
500.body: There is a scene that we will increasingly see in companies: someone connects an artificial intelligence agent to email, the calendar, the CRM, internal documentation, and perhaps also the billing system, and for a few minutes, they have the sensation of having found the perfect employee. If an agent should never delete documents, it is probably more reasonable not to give it the ability to delete them; if it can only work with amounts below a certain figure, the system itself can prevent any operation that exceeds that limit; and if certain communications need human review, they can be technically blocked until receiving approval. The one-hour test There is a simple question that any company could ask before putting an agent into production: if this agent malfunctioned for an hour without anyone noticing, what could it do?
